decisions.decision: The child's working directory is assigned in ProcessSupervisor and nowhere else, through one additive field, Dir string, whose zero value keeps today's behaviour exactly. SupervisedInvocationRunner does not assign it; it decides it, by reading Invocation.WorkingDirectory, validating it, and setting sup.Dir on its own copy of the supervisor value. Assignment and policy are split on purpose and the split is structural, not stylistic.
decisions.rationale: Measured: ProcessSupervisor is the only type in internal/runner that constructs an exec.Cmd (internal/runner/supervisor.go:56), so it is the only place a child directory can physically be assigned; SupervisedInvocationRunner never touches os/exec for the child at all -- it builds a value copy of the supervisor (sup := r.Supervisor at internal/runner/provider.go:357) and sets Stdin, Stdout and Env on it at :358-360 before calling sup.Run at :363. Putting the assignment anywhere but ProcessSupervisor would mean duplicating exec.Cmd construction, and putting the policy anywhere but SupervisedInvocationRunner would mean handing ProcessSupervisor a provider.Invocation it currently knows nothing about. The additive-field shape is the shape this type already uses three times: Env, Stdin and Stdout are all documented in the type comment (supervisor.go:16-33) as zero-value-compatible with every existing caller, and zero-value compatibility is required here rather than merely tidy, because three existing call sites construct a ProcessSupervisor with no directory and must keep passing unchanged under their own names: internal/runner/confinement_test.go:141, :189 and :214, and internal/api/live_local_test.go:159.

decisions.decision: An empty Invocation.WorkingDirectory is fail-closed: SupervisedInvocationRunner.Run returns a new sentinel, ErrInvocationWorkingDirectoryUnusable, and starts no process. It is NOT filled in from the Runner's own cwd. The refusal happens inside step (1) of Run's declared order -- the dependency check at internal/runner/provider.go:316-321, before LoadPreflightRecord and before Ledger.Reserve.
decisions.rationale: Using the Runner's cwd is the defect this task exists to remove, so making it the documented fallback would rename the defect rather than fix it, and would make the correct and the broken case indistinguishable from outside. It also costs nothing to refuse: internal/provider.Request.Validate already rejects an empty Workspace (internal/provider/provider.go:82-84) and all three Build functions set WorkingDirectory from req.Workspace through the one shared build helper (internal/provider/adapters.go:47), so an empty value is unreachable through the supported path; a refusal therefore converts an unreachable state into a loud one instead of into a silent default. The position of the check is load-bearing rather than incidental: dp-v2-017 d9's recorded risk is that a reservation debited before a failure stays charged at worst case forever, so a refusal placed after Ledger.Reserve would spend a real reservation to report a caller's own malformed request. Placing it with the other nil/empty checks also keeps the type's stated guarantee true -- that there is no field combination reaching the exec step with a dependency missing.

decisions.decision: The validation is fail-closed on five properties, all of them checkable without touching the child: the value must be non-empty; absolute; already canonical (filepath.Clean(dir) == dir, which rejects a '..' segment, a trailing separator and a doubled separator in one test); an existing directory by os.Stat; and not a symlink by os.Lstat. When Supervisor.Confine is non-nil it must additionally be the confinement workspace itself or a path beneath it. Nothing is repaired: every failure is the same sentinel with a distinct wrapped reason, and no process starts.
decisions.rationale: Each clause is derived from an existing, measured rule rather than invented. Absolute plus canonical is the pair NamespaceConfinement.wrap already enforces on Workspace (internal/runner/confinement.go:164-167) and the traversal-segment refusal the adapter already performs on the request (internal/provider/adapters.go:32-34, :105-113); re-checking it here is not redundancy but the second half of a boundary whose first half is on the other side of a package edge. The symlink clause is V2-016 A12's already-asserted property of the per-execution workspace, quoted in ev-v2-016-runner ('the workspace is not a symlink and is not group/world accessible'); a chdir into a symlink would put the child somewhere the argv guards never inspected. The Stat clause matters because exec's own chdir failure surfaces as a start error with no attribution, so checking first is what makes the message name the working directory rather than the executable. The Confine clause is the one that prevents a new contradiction: with Confine set, the kernel makes exactly one path read-write, and a cwd outside it would put the child where its own workspace is sealed -- which is not a widening but is a silent, self-contradictory state, so it is refused rather than repaired.

decisions.decision: With Confine non-nil, cmd.Dir is deliberately NOT used. The chdir is expressed inside the namespace, emitted by NamespaceConfinement.wrap as a single shQuote'd cd immediately after the two mount pairs and immediately before exec "$@" (internal/runner/confinement.go:170-176). wrap gains the directory as an argument and refuses -- returning an error, wrapping nothing, so ProcessSupervisor starts no child -- when it is not the workspace or beneath it. ProcessSupervisor assigns cmd.Dir only on the unconfined path.
decisions.rationale: This is forced by a fact about os/exec rather than chosen for elegance. Cmd.Dir is applied by chdir in the forked child before the exec, and with Confine set the program exec'ed is unshare (confinement.go:177), so a cmd.Dir can only ever take effect BEFORE the namespace exists and therefore before either mount pair -- it is structurally impossible for it to land after the read-write remount of the workspace. What the shell then inherits is a cwd reference into the mount that existed before step 1's bind-plus-read-only remount, not into the new mount object the seal was applied to, so relative resolution upward from that cwd ('../') walks the pre-seal mount. The in-namespace cd is the only ordering whose after-the-remount property is provable rather than inferred, which is why it is chosen regardless of what the measurement in A6 shows. Note also what this does NOT do, because non_goal 2 and non_goal 3 both bear on it: no mount is added, no path becomes reachable that was not reachable before, and the namespace is not being used as the thing that points the child at its workspace -- the cwd is now stated explicitly and independently of the mount topology, which is exactly the substitution the non_goal forbids being relied on.

decisions.decision: The codex -C and opencode --dir flags stay, and the resulting double expression of the workspace is judged NOT harmful -- but the judgement is made provable rather than assumed. Two new assertions carry it: in internal/provider, for all three adapters, Invocation.WorkingDirectory equals req.Workspace and equals the argv element immediately following that adapter's measured directory flag when one exists; in internal/runner, SupervisedInvocationRunner refuses fail-closed if Invocation.WorkingDirectory is not identical to that element. The unmeasured residual is named in writing and attributed.
decisions.rationale: non_goal 1 forbids removing a flag the CLI's own help declares, so the only question is whether keeping both is harmful, and the answer follows from where the two values come from: one call to the shared build helper produces both from the same req.Workspace (internal/provider/adapters.go:35-47), so they are the same string by construction, and V2-027 already measured that codex and opencode carry exactly one absolute path each while claude carries zero. For an absolute path equal to the cwd, a directory flag is idempotent: there is no relative-resolution difference to expose. What cannot be settled here is whether some future CLI version refuses when a directory flag and an inherited cwd disagree, or refuses when both are supplied at all -- measuring that needs the run subcommand executed, which this task's non_goal on Provider usage and V2-027's help-only rule both forbid, and which help declares nothing about either way. So the design keeps both, proves equality mechanically so that a disagreement is impossible rather than unlikely, refuses on disagreement so that a future divergence is loud, and records the CLI-refuses-both case as unmeasured and belonging to V2-028, which is the only exercise that runs codex and opencode at all.

decisions.decision: Live re-observation of the representative Provider is REQUIRED, for two independent reasons, and it is in this task's scope. It needs a new owner-approved provider-preflight record with its own task_id and its own limits.ledger_path; V2-075's record and ledger may not be reused, raised, or re-initialised.
decisions.rationale: Reason one is mechanical and is measured, not argued. ev-v2-075-provider-live-claude-rebind's freshness claim under gate rule G6b is the pair (observation commit d9f98ae573e617aafd82d87fa1c35f9bd6e26ffb, empty intersection between the diff since it and the published exercised file set). That set is the tracked artifact .agents/v2/evidence/artifacts/V2-075-live-exercise-files.json, 76 paths, and internal/runner/supervisor.go, internal/runner/provider.go, internal/runner/confinement.go and internal/provider/adapters.go are all inside its compiled group -- verified by reading the artifact. This task edits at least three of them, so the intersection becomes non-empty and the freshness claim lapses at the judging commit. G6b explicitly refuses the 'it was only a comment' argument, and here that argument is not even available. Reason two is semantic: the live exercise runs the real claude CLI through ProcessSupervisor{TermGrace: 3 * time.Second} with Confine nil (internal/runner/provider_live_test.go:218) against workspaces derived from the test's own temporary directory, so today the real child runs in the runner package's directory and after this task it runs in that ephemeral workspace. The observed behaviour changes, which is precisely the case re-observation exists for. On the record: V2-075's ledger stands at invocation_count 12 against max_invocations 12 with halted false, its own completion_conditions forbid raising a limit or re-initialising the ledger, and CostLedger.Reserve refuses a ledger whose recorded task_id disagrees with the run's -- so a new record is not a preference but the only path, and issuing one is an owner act the implementer may not transcribe.

decisions.decision: Three source comments and two documents currently state, as measured fact, something this task makes false, and correcting them is part of the change rather than follow-up: internal/provider/adapters.go:60-70, internal/provider/adapters_test.go:120-134, and the section of docs/operations/provider-adapters.md headed by the question whether the directory flags double Invocation.WorkingDirectory. The correction states the new fact and keeps the historical measurement visible rather than deleting it.
decisions.rationale: Those three places do not merely describe the old behaviour; they argue from it. adapters.go's comment justifies keeping the flags on the ground that ProcessSupervisor 'never assigns a child working directory', and provider-adapters.md's section concludes '二重表現ではない' from the same premise. Once the premise is false the conclusion is unsupported even though it stays correct for a different reason (d5), and a source comment that argues from a false measurement is worse than no comment: the next reader will trust it. Keeping the historical measurement with its date is the same discipline docs/operations/provider-live-claude.md already applies to the superseded V2-017 and V2-063 sections.

decisions.decision: A second field of provider.Invocation is set by the adapter and read by nobody, and this task records it and escalates rather than fixing it: SupervisedInvocationRunner never reads Invocation.Environment. Grant.Apply writes it (internal/runner/secret_broker.go:92-98) and only FakeInvocationRunner observes it; Run builds the child environment itself from the approved record's base names (internal/runner/provider.go:333-345) and passes that to sup.Env at :360. No behaviour changes here.
decisions.rationale: It is the identical defect shape as this task's own -- a field the adapter fills that the production execution path does not consume -- so finding it while measuring this one and not saying so would be the failure mode this task exists to correct. It is nevertheless not this task's outcome: the outcome names the working directory, and making a Secret Broker grant reach a real child process changes what the child may reach, which non_goal 3 forbids doing here and which needs its own credential-isolation acceptance rather than a rider. The defect is currently latent rather than active: every live exercise so far ran with granted_names empty (ev-v2-075's i3 check records a_granted_names_empty), so no grant has ever been dropped. The evidence must state the latency and the escalation together, because a reader who sees only 'unconsumed field' may assume credentials are already reaching children.

decisions.decision: V2-077 is OUTSIDE the surface-widening serialization chain and touches no chain file. It edits internal/runner, internal/provider, docs and the task ledger only. The common owner-console rule is deliberately disapplied and internal/web/** is prohibited.
decisions.rationale: The chain exists for the six file groups the surface tasks contend over -- the api handler, internal/application's ports, service and read models, contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml, internal/web/owner.{html,js} and both store adapters -- and this task's whole outcome is expressible without any of them: a child process's working directory is not a fact any read model reports. Appending an owner-console block would be the only reason to touch a chain file, and it would buy nothing: there is no owner-visible value to render, so the block would either be empty or would have to invent a surface, and inventing one would mean an openapi change, which puts the task in the chain and delays it behind V2-073, V2-068, V2-065 and V2-072 for no observable gain. The disapplication is recorded here so that it reads as a decision with a reason rather than as a forgotten constraint. The task does still move the runner, provider and docs component keys and must be serialized against any other task editing internal/runner or needing a live claude invocation, because the ledger and the subscription are single-holder resources.

decisions.decision: ci/components.json is not edited and no new import edge is created. supervisor.go gains no import; the validation lives in internal/runner/provider.go, which already imports os (:9) and path/filepath (:11); confinement.go already imports both. internal/provider gains no import at all, since d5's assertions are test-side and d7's change is a comment.
decisions.rationale: runner already declares provider among its dependencies and provider is a declared leaf with no dependencies, so the direction of every value that moves here is already declared. V2-045 has landed, which means internal/ci derives the import graph and turns a divergence from ci/components.json into a red make check rather than into silent drift: because this design creates no edge, a red manifest or dependency-coverage check means the design was departed from, and the right response is to stop and escalate rather than to edit the manifest. The one guard that could plausibly trip is internal/runner/source_guard_test.go:227, which pins ProcessSupervisor to exactly one referenced location in provider.go; setting a field on an existing value copy adds no reference to the type identifier, so the count is unchanged -- and that must be asserted rather than assumed.

decisions.decision: Determinism is preserved without a single new timing primitive. Every new unconfined assertion is made by running a child that reports its own cwd and exits; the confined assertions reuse confinement_test.go's existing bounded marker-file wait rather than introducing a second waiting idiom; the negative controls are refusals, which start no process and need no waiting at all.
decisions.rationale: The package's existing confinement tests already establish the only acceptable waiting shape in this area -- waitForConfinementMarker (internal/runner/confinement_test.go:31) is a bounded deadline poll over a file the child creates -- and adding a second shape would give a later reader two idioms to choose between, one of which will eventually be a sleep. The majority of this task's assertions are refusals rather than executions, which is a property of the fail-closed design rather than a convenience: a refusal is the cheapest deterministic assertion available, since no process, no clock and no filesystem race is involved.

decisions.decision: The confinement measurement in A6 is a measurement with two admissible outcomes, not a prediction to be confirmed. The implementer measures, with a positive control, whether a relative upward write from a cwd inherited across namespace creation reaches the pre-seal mount, records whichever result the kernel gives, and does not change the design on the basis of it.
decisions.rationale: The design is already settled by d4's structural argument -- cmd.Dir cannot land after the remount when the exec'd program is unshare -- so the measurement is there to establish whether the rejected ordering is merely unprovable or actually exploitable, which is a materially different sentence to write in the evidence and in runner-local.md. Writing the stronger sentence without measuring would be a fabricated verification, and writing the weaker one when the stronger is true would understate a containment gap. Making the two outcomes admissible in advance is what stops the implementer from tuning the test until it agrees with the packet.

risks: The representative Provider's live behaviour changes: the real claude child moves from the Runner's own directory into the Increment's ephemeral workspace. A CLI that reads project-scoped configuration or asks a trust question about its cwd could behave differently there, and no measurement in this repository has ever run it in an empty workspace. This is the reason re-observation is scope rather than paperwork, and if the re-observed exercise fails for that reason the correct response is to stop and escalate, not to widen what the child may reach.

The live re-observation depends on an owner act. A new provider-preflight record must be issued and approved before a single invocation, because V2-075's ledger is at 12 of 12 and its own completion conditions forbid raising the limit or re-initialising it. If the record does not exist the implementer must stop with the code and unit evidence landed and the live item recorded as not run, and must never record it as passed.

Setting the child's directory changes the meaning of every relative path the child resolves, including any relative path a Provider CLI writes into its own state. Nothing in this repository passes a relative path to a child today -- the adapter guards refuse a traversal segment and V2-027 measured that only absolute workspaces appear in argv -- but the change is silent for anything that does, so the evidence must state the new resolution base explicitly rather than only that the directory is now set.

d8's second unconsumed field, Invocation.Environment, means a Secret Broker grant does not reach a real child process today. Recording it makes it visible; leaving it unfixed means a later task may assume this one closed the class. The escalation must name the owner and must state that the defect is latent only because every live exercise so far had granted_names empty.

Editing internal/provider/adapters.go, even by a comment only, moves the provider component key and puts a path in the V2-075 exercised set. That is unavoidable given d7 -- a comment that argues from a now-false measurement is worse than no comment -- but it means the re-observation cannot be avoided by confining the change to internal/runner either.
